result.delta_one_sentence: A keeps the tasks, instructions, checkers and OS shell fixed in English and changes only interface text language and layout direction, independently, in one checked config file, so the right-to-left effect splits into additive text and layout parts with intervals and a reachable equivalence null; B localizes the whole OS and the instructions at once, so it can only observe an untested drop and guess at its cause.
result.reasoning: Both designs study one phenomenon: computer-use agents may do worse when the interface is localized right-to-left. The mechanisms differ. B is a broad observational benchmark (about 200 tasks, 30 apps, 5 languages, 6 agents, one run per cell). In its right-to-left condition, script, translated strings, mirrored layout, OS shell localization and (in the matched condition) instruction language all change together. It offers two candidate causes, the visual complexity of the script and the mirrored layout, but has no condition that separates them. It reports no intervals or significance tests, even though the gap is small (13.7% vs 19.3%) and each cell has one run. A is a controlled factorial intervention aimed at exactly the question B leaves open. A 2x2 of text language by layout direction is set by one system file, and everything else is held fixed. It adds pre-run oracles that each switch does only its job: chrome mirrors and documents do not, window titles stay identical, translated strings that leak into documents (such as the default sheet name) are pinned so checkers are not broken by translation, and pixel boxes replace unreliable accessibility boxes under mirroring. It runs a census of eligible tasks with no selection on agent success, repeats episodes across two scaffolds, and decomposes the total change exactly into the two main effects. Its primary decision uses a dual equivalence margin, with simulated power for both a robustness null and a 15% relative harm, plus moderators that test which route carries any effect. A is the stronger causal contribution: a null or a clean attribution from A is interpretable, and B's numbers are not. A's weaknesses are external validity and ecological realism. It covers one office suite, one right-to-left language, an English OS shell and two scaffolds. The Arabic-text-in-left-to-right cell is not a configuration real users see. Its moderators are correlational. B's strengths are breadth, a reusable multi-app, multi-language resource and a separate safety subset, but as evidence about why right-to-left hurts agents it adds little beyond a plausible hypothesis and an anecdote. Net: A tests B's guess with a design that can actually support or reject it, so A is the stronger research contribution on this question. B is the wider benchmark.

Feasibility.lens: Feasibility: is the first step's pilot decisive, and can the step run on 8xH100 within its budget using the assets that exist today?
Feasibility.strongest_argument:
The first step is Phase 0. Its job is to decide the gates K0 (at least 62 tasks admitted) and K1 (the D53 delta certification, P0.6). The pilot that ran cannot decide either gate, and the run that could decide them cannot start with the assets that exist.

Why the pilot does not decide K0 or K1:
- No real Arabic string was ever rendered. In the 106-task sweep (jobs 1099/1100) the "pseudo-Arabic" cell L4 had no catalogs, so its strings fell back to English (compute/pilot/s2v3_pilot_b.py lines 13-14). That cell is English text in a mirrored layout.
- The ar-LTR cell, one of the four Phase 1 cells, never ran at any task state. It ran only on blank documents (L5 in job 1098).
- The pilot ran in the LO-VM container, not in the VM lane on a derived image.
- The registered oracle was not implemented: no O2 ink identity, no O3 on ink-located boxes, no O6, no positive controls, no mirror specification.
  - O3 on AT-SPI was abandoned: job 1100 found 53% of matched elements keep unmirrored extents.
  - O5 was "not claimed". At residual < 0.02 more documents matched the flipped image (34) than the unflipped one (15) (job1099/pilot-b-analysis.json).
- Even the switch location differs from the registered one. The pilot inserted its own xcsxcu layer after the res: layer (job1098/pilot-record.json, prepare.fundamentalrc_after). The registration writes the selector into /etc/libreoffice/registry, which is the same layer as main.xcd.

Why the decisive run cannot start:
- It needs three package downloads. That is an outward action waiting on Kevin.
- It needs image-surgery code that is not written or reviewed.
- It needs a lane version that accepts a new image digest and the 27 reserve tasks (lane.py:90 pins QCOW2_SHA256; line 253 allows only pool and dev tasks).
- It needs a registered deviation of q2-action-path-v2 for P0.6, which does not exist.
- It needs a way to give each VM its own cell, and none exists or is designed. The VM container bind-mounts one pinned qcow2 read-only per manifest (harness/q2/vm/driver.py:133). The four cells "assigned to VM slots at random" therefore need either four images or a runtime write to /etc as root in the guest, through the guest server that D53 does not certify. The registration also needs LANGUAGE=ar in the Arabic cells' LibreOffice process (P0.3). That has no mechanism and contradicts "the cells differ only in one selector file". Neither gap is listed among the proposal's blockers.

By the gauntlet's compute rule the pilot is also not an orx node, so it does not count as an executable pilot and the 79 cap binds.

Phase 1's fit under 8 GPU-h rests on a cap rule nobody has adopted. Under S1a's registered c_proj the same 1,696 episodes are 19.1 GPU-h (registration lines 431-432). The design study (section 5) says "A successor registration needs that rule adopted", and D22 says expected use never replaces a cap. The Phase 1 manifest does not exist and has no dry run (proposal line 400; doctor: "compute lacks a hashed Slurm manifest", "slurm_test did not pass").

The owner's own forecast puts reaching Phase 1 at 0.6 x 0.65 x 0.85, about 0.33.
Feasibility.what_would_change_my_mind:
All of the following would change my verdict:

result.delta_one_sentence: B takes the effect A reports but cannot attribute (agents doing worse on a right-to-left localized desktop) and splits it inside one office suite, setting interface language and layout direction independently while the instructions, checkers and shell stay in English, adding a cell that only shuffles toolbar buttons to test whether the effect is about direction or just moved controls, and checking validity before any agent runs, at the cost of A's breadth and with the runs on real translations not yet done.
result.reasoning:
Same mechanism: both ask why a localized right-to-left interface lowers a screenshot-driven agent's success, and both suspect the script, the mirrored layout or both. A names these causes but changes them all at once; B is built to tell them apart. The difference is in the method, not in the hypothesis.

A's strengths: it is a broad artifact that already exists, with about 200 tasks, about 30 applications, 5 languages and 6 agents, and its results are in. That makes it a useful resource.

A's weaknesses: its causal claim has no support. Switching the system language changes the script, the translated strings, the layout direction, the shell and every application together. Its 'matched' condition also changes the instruction language, so it does not isolate anything either. The headline gap of about 5 points (14% against 19%) comes from one run per cell, averaged over agents, with no intervals or tests; episodes from the same task are correlated, so the gap could be noise. The instructions are machine-translated, which adds another variable that differs across languages. The appendix example of a click landing where an unmirrored control would sit is an anecdote, not evidence.

B's strengths: it uses a real 2x2 design (text by direction) inside one application, with everything else held in English. The layout and text main effects add up to the total change by construction. The shuffled-toolbar cell is a well-chosen control: it tests whether mirroring itself matters or whether any relocation of familiar controls does the same damage. The validity work is strong. Before any agent runs, a render oracle reads element positions from pixels, includes planted positive controls, and checks the English configuration against the unmodified application. The benchmark's own checker re-scores each task's reference answer and empty start in every cell, so a configuration that would change a verdict by itself is caught. Tasks are chosen by fixed rules blind to outcomes, and decisions use pre-set two-sided equivalence margins, with a ratio margin that never-solved tasks cannot dilute.

B's weaknesses:
- **Narrow scope.** One application, one language pair, and a partially localized setup (Arabic app inside an English shell). English text in a mirrored layout is a configuration real users never see, so how far the results generalize is limited.
- **Interaction hidden.** Main effects that add up to the total can hide an interaction between text and direction. That interaction should be reported separately.
- **Likely underpowered.** With 106 tasks and 4 episodes per cell split over two scaffolds, the standard error of the paired difference is probably around 3 points. Against a 5-point margin, and an even tighter 15% ratio margin at low solve rates, an equivalence conclusion will often come out inconclusive. The shuffled cell gets only 2 episodes per task, so the 'direction-specific' comparison is weaker still.
- **Unfinished.** The shipped Arabic translations, the virtual-machine image that carries them and the re-certification of the input path on that image have not run. The only check so far is a CPU pilot with a generated stand-in script.

Verdict: as a research design and a scientific contribution to the causal question, B is clearly stronger. It answers the question A leaves open, and its results would be interpretable whichever way they came out, null included. A is the more complete deliverable today and the better benchmark resource, but its explanatory claim does not hold up.

candidate.mechanism_paragraph: A paired measurement of how a localized right-to-left interface changes a screenshot-driven computer-use agent's success, made inside one executable desktop benchmark and deliberately narrower than localizing a whole operating system. For one office suite whose tasks, documents, instructions, checkers and operating-system shell stay in English, one system-level configuration file sets two factors independently: the application's interface language (English or Arabic, through both of the application's language keys) and its layout direction (left-to-right or mirrored, through the application's own direction key). A fifth cell keeps English left-to-right and only puts each toolbar's buttons in a fixed random order, a relocation of the most-clicked controls with no change of direction. The measurement is a census of the benchmark's office-suite tasks that pass fixed rules blind to outcomes (106 candidates): four episodes per task and cell (two in the rearranged cell), split across two agent scaffolds, in one session. The layout and text main effects sum to the total change. The layout effect is reported as a net change on these tasks, decided with a dual equivalence margin (5 points absolute and a 15% ratio of solve rates, which never-solved tasks cannot dilute); it may be called direction-specific only if the mirrored cell does worse than the rearranged cell across tasks. Before any model runs, every cell is compared with English left-to-right at each task's starting screen by a render oracle (element positions located from pixels rather than accessibility extents, text-run identity, document identity, window titles, the English configuration against the unmodified application, planted positive controls), and each task's reference answer and empty starting state are saved in every cell and re-scored by the benchmark's own checker, so a task is excluded only where a cell would change a verdict without any agent. Feasibility.lens: Feasibility: after the D74 repair, is the first step (Phase 0: K0 admission plus instrument checks, and K1, the D53 delta certification) decisive, and can it run within budget with the assets that exist today?
Feasibility.strongest_argument:
The first step is Phase 0. Its job is to decide two gates: K0 (at least 62 tasks admitted, with every instrument check holding) and K1 (the D53 delta certification, P0.6). After the repair, neither gate is decided in a way that could license Phase 1. The run that would decide them cannot start with the assets that exist.

1. The one K0 verdict made under rules committed before the data is FAIL.
- The orx node of record reports status PHASE0_K0_FAIL, with c04_positive_controls FAIL and c10_k0_admission FAIL; the host replicate 1132 agrees. Synthetic plants were caught on 101 of 106 tasks for O3 and 95 of 106 for O2, against the committed 100% bar.
- Under the kill criterion the proposal itself states ("K0 fewer than 62 admitted tasks or a failed instrument check (infrastructure exit)"), the pilot's outcome is an exit, not a go.
- The proposal does not take that exit. It does two things instead:
  - It adds an admission rule chosen after seeing the proxy's 53 admitted tasks: c13 and decide_checker_invariance, added in da45543, which yields 105.
  - In v3.1 it replaces I1's bar with "a bar fixed before Phase 0 proper" (registration lines 273-275 and 318-319). That leaves the K0 gate as registered with a free parameter, to be set by someone who already knows the stand-in's 95% and 90% detection rates.
- Even the "committed rules" verdict was not computed with the committed code. phase0.py was committed in c8669d2 at 10:01 UTC, and the sweep 1131 ran from 10:03 to 10:18 UTC. The calibration and the plants then changed in da45543: dy_vcl estimation, tol3, plant dx = tol3+8, and the O2 plant restricted to already-identical runs. The change is disclosed as finishing the oracle's code before its first output.
- So the pilot cannot honestly be said to pass K0, and v3.1 leaves K0 undecidable until a number is chosen.

2. K1 has no executed component in the VM lane.
- What the CPU lane showed (a `us` keymap and postconfig saves in a container under openbox) is not the D53 runtime. D53's scope excludes another image, untested catalog instances and the guest server under task applications.

3. The run that decides both gates cannot start. I verified each blocker:
- The three Launchpad downloads wait on Kevin (D74).
- No image-surgery code exists. Searching the repo for debugfs or dpkg-deb finds only the q2-mutation vmprobe extractor.
- No per-slot cell lane code exists. lane.py:90 and :189 pin QCOW2_SHA256, and lane.py:253 admits only pool and dev tasks, which leaves out the 27 reserve tasks. driver.py:133 bind-mounts a single regular file at /System.qcow2, so the "five pinned qcow2 overlays" must either be flattened images or need the driver changed to mount a backing chain. The registration says neither.
- No lane-side capture, oracle or checker-invariance code exists. capture.py is container-only, yet K1 item (d) requires both on the overlays.
- No registered deviation of q2-action-path-v2 exists.
- P0.6 alone is about 44 VM-hours. The lane recapture of 106 tasks times the cells, and the 1,110 lane saves, are not costed at all.

4. Even granted all of that, the pilot's numbers do not carry over:
- They come from a generated stand-in catalog of matched length, not the shipped catalog. The proposal says so: "the leak, coverage and O5 numbers are the stand-in's".
- They come from a container with a different window manager: a 23 px VCL offset, and the window bottom 3-4 px off screen. So dy and tol3 = 20 px must be re-frozen in the lane.
- The 105 count rests on an admission test that is blind on a sixth of the census. On 17 of the 105 admitted tasks, A4 compares only end states that fail in every cell: 12 have only a do-nothing state, and 5 have golds that fail everywhere. On those tasks it cannot detect a cell that turns a correct solution into a failure.

5. Phase 1's fit under 8 GPU-h rests on a cap rule nobody has adopted.
- Under the design study's rule it is 6.83 GPU-h. Under S1a's registered c_proj it is 21.5 GPU-h. D22 says "expected use never replaces a cap".
- The Compute doctor is FAIL: no Phase 1 manifest, dry run, test-only or S2 model loop. By the gauntlet rule, a failed doctor blocks promotion whatever the score.
- The owner's own forecast puts reaching Phase 1 at about 0.3.

Points in the candidate's favour, which I checked:
- The orx node exists, with ORX_RESULT exit=0, which addresses the 79 cap.
- The GPU cap holds by construction. The cap passes 8 GPU-h only at a slot of 233 s, and K8 truncation still leaves K = 90 at 233 s and 70 at 300 s, both at least 62.

Identification.lens: Identification: after the repair, are the first step's verdicts (the Phase 0 admission and instrument verdicts, plus the Phase 1 decision labels the step registers) produced by the estimator, the design or artefacts rather than by the mechanism they claim to measure?
Identification.strongest_argument:
The repair fixes the total effect but not the mechanism readings. Census D, read as the net change in success under mirroring (P3), is identified: cells are randomized within one session. I also looked for direction-coupled saved content that could fake a D effect in the 7.3.7.2 source and found none in the output formats these tasks use. Every reading added to attach a mechanism, and the passing K0 count, is produced by the design or by the estimator:

(1) MIRROR_SPECIFIC (E_dir = en-RTL minus placebo) does not isolate direction.
- The claim "false MIRROR_SPECIFIC 0.023-0.027 under every direction-free scenario" holds only because power-v4.py defines "direction-free" as giving the placebo the same effect structure and size as the mirror (docstring lines 29-31; SCENARIOS lines 311-327).
- The pilot measured the placebo as a much smaller change (C52): 53% of chrome moved by 271 px against all of it by 991 px. In E-PL, 22 of 22 menus are unmoved, and the document offset is 0 (mirroring shifts it by about 59 px).
- I ran the registered decide() unchanged, with a direction-free uniform 15% harm whose placebo share is scaled by the measured displacement. MIRROR_SPECIFIC fires in 0.336 of replicates at 0.27 (271/991) and 0.441 at 0.145 (53% x 271/991). A purely mirror-specific harm gives 0.555. NO_EXCESS is only 0.17-0.24.
- The script's own "mirror -30%, placebo -15%" row is a pure magnitude contrast, yet it is labelled "specific".
- So MIRROR_SPECIFIC and P8 mostly test displacement dose. ScreenHaystack-style relocation, the proposal's own cause (i), is direction-free and produces them.

(2) The mechanism moderators are effectively application indicators, created by the oracle's tolerance.
- Application explains 85% of the variance in O8's per-task count. The within-application SD is 0.45-1.18 elements, and Calc has 21 on 42 of 46 tasks.
- Of 2,118 O8 entries, 2,044 come from elements that are out of spec on at least 90% of that application's tasks.
- 1,408 entries are elements that were located, with |dx| deciles of 13-24 px (median 24). That is just beyond tol3 = 20, which is the 95th percentile of a 24-px calibration window (phase0.py lines 118 and 139).
- The registered T moderator, the Arabic chrome share, has within-application SD of at most 0.004 (Writer 0.989 on every task).
- So the "RTL defects" row and any chrome-share slope would be contrasts between three applications, carrying everything else that differs between them. The regressions have no application term, and task-level CR2 treats the 105 tasks as if they were independent.

(3) The passing K0 count comes from an estimator chosen after the committed one failed.
- Under the committed rule, 53 tasks are admitted (Calc 42, Impress 8, Writer 3). Under the checker-invariance rule chosen afterwards, 105 are (46, 39, 20).
- 22 of the 105 have no positive control. For 17, the only check is a do-nothing state that fails in all six cells. For 5, no result file exists in any cell (saved = null), so they pass the file-identity fallback vacuously.
- Two of those five, 0f84bef9 and f178a4a9, are C1 tasks. The registration admits C1 tasks only if P0.10 passes, and P0.10 never ran.
- The title rule A2 was also relaxed after the sweep: 936321ce is admitted only under the relaxed rule.
- The I3 and I4 passes (212/212 and 943/943) follow from how the stand-in catalog is built: one Arabic letter per Latin letter, with the same keys. P7 compares two routes into the same VCL flag.
Identification.what_would_change_my_mind:
Each item below removes one prong:
- A placebo matched in dose before data. For example, a direction-free rearrangement that moves menus, toolbars, the sidebar and the document region by the mirror's measured displacement profile. Alternatively, MIRROR_SPECIFIC is renamed a magnitude contrast, and the 0.023-0.027 claim is replaced by its rate under dose-scaled direction-free harms (0.34-0.44).
- O8 rebuilt as a defect measure that varies within an application, or the moderator regressions given application fixed effects. Either way, a stated rule that no mechanism is named from a slope identified only between applications.
- K0 decided only on the committed rule, or the checker-invariance rule frozen before Phase 0 proper and applied to the shipped catalogs. It would require a passing gold (or an agent-made probe output) for every admitted task, P0.10 run before C1 tasks enter, and the vacuous fallback removed.
- I3 and I4 shown to pass with the real Arabic catalog.

Novelty.strongest_argument:
I refute on the "trivial recombination" prong only. The "already published" prong fails again, and I concede it.

1. Not published. My 10 counted orx discover queries found no study that crosses interface text language with layout direction for any GUI agent or VLM. Together with wave 1's 21 refuter queries and the repair's 6, the queries covered:
   - RTL scripts other than Arabic (Hebrew and Persian).
   - Multilingual GUI grounding.
   - OSWorld perturbation studies.
   - The very recent window (after 2026-09-15).
   - Placebo-style layout permutation.
   - Pseudolocalization.

2. The repair's own text concedes that every design component is prior art, and that the residual is a number rather than a design:
   - Line 270: "The residual is narrow and is a measurement, not a method."
   - Lines 273-275: "the census frame, the oracle, the isolation mechanism, the off-diagonal cells and the paired-variant method are prior art used as infrastructure."
   - Line 133: "S2 does not answer that split."
   - Line 258: the oracle is "not a novelty claim", at confidence "high".
   - doctors-r1/novelty.json: "The delta is a measurement, not a method."

   Wave 1's novelty refuter asked for exactly this restatement in its condition (a). But the restatement fixes the wording, not the substance: a fresh measurement made by recombining prior-art parts is the definition of the objection.

3. This gauntlet judges only Phase 0, and Phase 0 produces nothing outside prior art. Its outputs are:
   - A filtered OSWorld subset: 117 tasks, the same Calc/Impress/Writer counts as OSWorld's Table 10, minus 11.
   - A pseudolocalized catalog. The proposal's own C22 and line 121-122 cite Windows' mirrored pseudo-locale and en-XB/qps-plocm as standard test practice.
   - An oracle in the GWALI/ITDroid/RotDroid/IBM tradition.
   - A checker re-score.

   The only output that is not prior art is the D and T numbers. Those come from Phase 1, which D24 and D70 keep outside this gauntlet.

4. The repair's one new design element, the PL placebo, recombines a published perturbation family using textbook sham-control logic:
   - Relocating controls as a GUI-agent perturbation is already published: VAF's position family (cited as "Yu et al., 2026" by PAIR 2610.07972, line 34); UI-Verse 2605.02729 (full read, lines 296-301: "CUAs often struggle when equivalent controls shift position", with paired baseline and revised UIs); ScreenHaystack relocation; GUI-Perturbed; and PAIR's user-conditioned layouts.
   - The proposal concedes the placebo is not matched in magnitude: 53% of chrome elements moved by a median 271 px, against 100% and 991 px for mirroring. It "controls for rearranging the toolbars, not for an equally large change."

5. The factors and much of the measured object are already published:
   - macOSWorld names the factor pair word for word (full text line 527: "Arabic glyphs or the mirrored UI layout, or both").
   - Its Table 6 already gives the English-instruction total in the Arabic environment, which is S2's ar-RTL minus en: 33.3% to 22.8% for OpenAI CUA.
   - The same table gives non-RTL, non-Latin-script contrasts: zh 29.8% and ja 31.0%. A rough script-versus-Arabic triangulation can already be read from it.
   - Paired, task- and grader-preserving interface variants for CUAs are a crowded design family: VAF, WebPageBench, BreakingWeb, GUI vs CLI 2606.24551 ("identical goals, states, and final-state verifiers"), PAIR, UI-Verse, and Same Tasks Different Apps 2609.34139.

6. None of wave 1's withdrawal conditions is met:
   - (b) is not met: still one model family, application-level only, no shell or system-locale factor, no Arabic-instruction factor.
   - (c) is not met. The repair's confound findings are:
     - `ooLocale` alone leaves registry labels in English (C40).
     - Localized defaults reach saved files in 34 tasks (C49).
     - Impress placeholder prompts change the slide in 14 of 40 tasks (C48).

     These were shown on a generated stand-in, not the shipped catalogs, and were found by a tagged pseudo-catalog, which is standard pseudolocalization. Checker invariance (1,110 verdicts, no change) shows they bias no checker outcome. The proposal claims no construction contribution and shows no published result to be biased.
   - (d) is not met: nobody has published an attempt to separate script from direction that failed.

   If uncertain, I default to refuted.
Novelty.what_would_change_my_mind:
Any one of these would make me withdraw the refutation or reduce it to a wording note.

(a) A recorded ruling that the program's bar accepts a measurement-only delta, i.e. a new number from a recombination of prior-art components. This would be Kevin's ruling under D24, or the blind critic and a provider-distinct reviewer of this run explicitly saying so. The novelty lens would then not apply to this kind of proposal.

(b) The measured object reaching macOSWorld's open split within the 8 GPU-h line. For example: crossing system or shell locale and direction too, adding a matched Arabic-instruction factor, or adding a second model family.

(c) Evidence that the construction is itself a contribution. This means a demonstration on the shipped Arabic catalogs that the naive switches give confounded cells, for example `ooLocale` alone giving a mixed-language interface, or localized defaults reaching content a checker reads. Standard pseudolocalization and mirroring checks would have to miss this, and it would have to bias a published GUI-agent locale result such as macOSWorld's. The proposal would also have to claim and credit that construction.

(d) A published GUI-agent or VLM study that tried to separate script from direction and failed, or said it could not be done.

A broader search alone (a CJK-capable venue index, or a refresh of macOSWorld's citers) would only firm up "not published". It would not answer the recombination objection.
